title: Municipal funding appeal and Kinsmen site redevelopment
subtitle: Also: budget amendment deadline, GRT bus wraps, Duke Street cycle tracks, climate funding agreement, future hybrid shelter sites.
overview: Regional Council asked the Province and the federal government to create a new municipal funding framework, arguing that property taxes cannot pay for the services and infrastructure that a growing region needs. Council added a public forum with area MPPs and MPs in early 2024 {{vote:m8}}, and approved the full motion {{vote:m7}}.

Council directed staff to explore redeveloping the former Kinsmen Children's Centre site in Cambridge as a multi-use building with paramedic services and affordable housing, and it specifically excluded a homeless shelter. Staff said the work is at an early stage, with community consultation to come. Council also set December 4 at noon as the deadline for written motions to amend the 2024 budget {{vote:m13}}.

Other approvals included a $13.7 million contract for security upgrades at water and facilities buildings, cycle tracks on Duke Street in Kitchener, a five-year ClimateActionWR agreement, and a small Official Plan exception in New Dundee. Council also gave informal direction, without a motion, for staff to begin looking at sites for another hybrid shelter. Some councillors opposed this.

decisions.detail: Council asked the Province and federal government to commit to a new municipal funding framework and review, and to circulate the request to other municipalities, MPs, MPPs, AMO and FCM {{vote:m7}}.
Staff will explore a multi-use building with paramedic services and affordable housing, excluding any homeless shelter, and apply for an FCM sustainable affordable housing study grant.
Motions to amend the final 2024 budget must be submitted in writing by noon on December 4, 2023, with late motions allowed only if the committee dispenses with notice by a two-thirds vote.

Council adopted a Official Plan exception for six lots at 63 Benjamin Street in New Dundee, referred GRT advertising policy changes back to staff, extended the Truth and Reconciliation bus wrap to February 29, 2024, and approved Duke Street cycle tracks.
Council accepted the Fire Monitoring of Canada proposal for water and facilities building security upgrades, estimated at $13,713,069.75 plus taxes.
Council approved a $475,000 expropriation settlement for 255 King Street, Cambridge, and a development charge settlement, with authority for similar rental housing agreements.
Council authorized a new five-year collaborative agreement with Reep Green Solutions and Sustainable Waterloo Region to run ClimateActionWR.
Council endorsed and submitted comments to the Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing on proposed Development Charges Act regulations.

debate: On the fiscal framework, one councillor argued that sending letters to Queen's Park rarely produces action, so a face-to-face forum with MPPs and MPs would help them understand the Region's pressures. Another councillor said the main motion was stronger without it.

Some councillors said advocacy already happens through heads of Council, AMO, FCM and big-city mayors' groups, and worried a forum could become partisan blame rather than produce solutions. Supporters said it was a chance to set partisanship aside and bring solutions.

On 651 Concession Road, delegates were concerned about traffic, nearby schools and a lack of communication, and said they had heard it would be a homeless shelter. Councillors said a shelter was never proposed and backed the exclusion wording. Staff said consultation with the City and community would follow.

On the budget deadline, one councillor argued that a November 29 cut-off came before the last budget day before the final meeting. December 4 gave members the weekend to consider the results while still giving staff and the public notice.

On future hybrid shelter sites, supporters said finding a site took months last time, so work should start now. Others wanted to wait for the plan to end chronic homelessness and data on the Erbs Road site first. Staff said starting early would help.
